<!-- The stylesheets the page needs. Without a build step it is `<link>`, not
     `import`: a browser does not resolve a package name. -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@lo-tek/interfaces@VERSION/src/tokens/tokens.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@lo-tek/interfaces@VERSION/src/components/standalone/connection-status/connection-status.css">
<!-- Or everything in one file: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@lo-tek/interfaces@VERSION/dist/lotek.css -->

<lt-connection-status class="lt-connection-status" role="status" aria-live="polite" data-ignore-morph></lt-connection-status>

<!-- Once for the whole app, in the page template. Not once per component. -->
<script type="module">
  import { defineLtConnectionStatus } from
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@lo-tek/interfaces@VERSION/dist/components/standalone/connection-status/lt-connection-status.js"

  defineLtConnectionStatus()
</script>

<script type="module">
  import { reportFailure, reportSuccess } from
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@lo-tek/interfaces@VERSION/dist/components/standalone/connection-status/lt-connection-status.js"

  const connection = document.querySelector("lt-connection-status")
  if (!connection) throw new Error("element not found")

  // The page's own saves go through this function, so every answer from the
  // server, or the lack of one, is reported. A module keeps its names to
  // itself, so it is put on window, where the page's other scripts call it
  // with what they save.
  // A request that got no answer is a lost connection, and so is an answer
  // from a gateway whose server is gone (502, 503, 504). Any other answer, an
  // error status included, means the server is there. reportSuccess and
  // reportFailure wait for the component to be registered, and warn when it
  // never is; the save does not wait for them.
  window.saveRoute = async (body) => {
    let response
    try {
      response = await fetch("/api/routes", { method: "POST", body })
    } catch {}
    if (response && ![502, 503, 504].includes(response.status)) reportSuccess(connection)
    else reportFailure(connection)
    return response
  }
</script>

// src/lotek.d.ts, gives <lt-connection-status> types in JSX
import "@lo-tek/interfaces/react-jsx"

<!-- The stylesheets the page needs. Without a build step it is `<link>`, not
     `import`: a browser does not resolve a package name. -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@lo-tek/interfaces@VERSION/src/tokens/tokens.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@lo-tek/interfaces@VERSION/src/components/standalone/connection-status/connection-status.css">
<!-- Or everything in one file: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@lo-tek/interfaces@VERSION/dist/lotek.css -->

<!-- Once for the whole app, in the page template. Not once per component. -->
<script type="module">
  import { defineLtConnectionStatus } from
    "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@lo-tek/interfaces@VERSION/dist/components/standalone/connection-status/lt-connection-status.js"

  defineLtConnectionStatus()
</script>

<!-- Datastar itself, after the registration: module scripts run in the
     order they stand, so no request goes out before the web component
     exists. Without it the `data-` attributes below do nothing. -->
<script type="module"
        src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/starfederation/datastar@v1.0.4/bundles/datastar.js"></script>

<!-- Datastar sends `datastar-fetch` on the document for every request.
     `retrying`: the request got no answer. `error`: an answer of 400 or
     more, with its status; 502, 503 and 504 come from a gateway whose
     server is gone, any other is a server that is there. A patch arrived,
     so the stream is alive; `finished` is no good as a sign, since it also
     comes after an error. An answer without content, like 204, or with
     `text/javascript`, says neither, and the next patch clears the bar. -->
<lt-connection-status class="lt-connection-status" role="status" aria-live="polite" data-ignore-morph
                      data-on:datastar-fetch__document="evt.detail.type === 'retrying' || [502, 503, 504].includes(+evt.detail.argsRaw.status) ? el.reportFailure() : (evt.detail.type === 'error' || evt.detail.type.startsWith('datastar-patch')) && el.reportSuccess()"></lt-connection-status>

<script type="module">
  const messages = document.getElementById("messages")

  document.getElementById("restart").addEventListener("click", async () => {
    let answer
    try {
      answer = await fetch("/relays/14/restart", { method: "POST" })
    } catch {}
    // A gateway whose server is gone answers 502, 503 or 504, which is no
    // answer from the relay either. Any other answer that is not ok means
    // the server is there and said no.
    if (answer && [502, 503, 504].includes(answer.status)) answer = undefined
    // fetch follows a redirect, as to the log-in page when the session has
    // run out, and the page it lands on is ok. That is no restart.
    if (answer?.ok && !answer.redirected) {
      messages.show("Relay 14 is back", { color: "success" })
    } else if (answer) {
      messages.show("Relay 14 refused the restart. Try again.", { color: "danger", duration: 0 })
    } else {
      messages.show("Relay 14 did not answer. Try again.", { color: "danger", duration: 0 })
    }
  })
</script>

<html lang="en" data-theme={theme}>

<!-- In <head>, without defer, before the page is drawn -->
<script>
  const stored = localStorage.getItem("theme")
  if (stored === "light" || stored === "dark") {
    document.documentElement.dataset.theme = stored
  }
</script>

<script type="module">
  const stored = localStorage.getItem("theme")
  const chosen = stored === "light" || stored === "dark" ? stored : "auto"

  for (const button of document.querySelectorAll(".lt-theme-control")) {
    button.checked = button.value === chosen

    button.addEventListener("change", () => {
      localStorage.setItem("theme", button.value)
      // The attribute from the script in <head> has to go, or it stands in
      // front of "Follow the system", which has no theme block to win with.
      delete document.documentElement.dataset.theme
    })
  }
</script>
